## Acceptance Criteria

<!--
List requirements for the documentation update.
Include details such as clarity, accuracy, completeness, accessibility, code examples, screenshots, links to standards, etc.
-->

- [ ] Documentation is clear, accurate, and up-to-date
- [ ] Follows [WordPress documentation standards](https://developer.wordpress.org/coding-standards/inline-documentation/)
- [ ] Includes code examples/screenshots if applicable
- [ ] Documentation is accessible and easy to find
- [ ] Changelog entry prepared for PR if user-facing update

### Definition of Ready (DoR)

<!--
Checklist items to ensure the request is ready for work.
-->

- [ ] Documentation need is clear and well-defined
- [ ] Related docs/issues or files linked
- [ ] Acceptance criteria listed
- [ ] Estimate added if relevant
- [ ] Milestone/release assigned (if applicable)

### Definition of Done (DoD)

<!--
Checklist items to ensure the documentation update is complete and actionable.
-->

- [ ] Documentation meets org standards and guidelines
- [ ] Changelog entry prepared for PR (CHANGELOG.md)
- [ ] Documentation reviewed for clarity and accessibility
- [ ] Screenshots/code examples included if relevant
- [ ] PR uses correct branch prefix (docs/)

## Directions & Next Steps

<!--
Instructions for contributors and maintainers.
-->

- Double-check all details, requirements, links, and references above.
- For any related PR, use the branch prefix `docs/` (see [Branching Strategy](../AUTOMATION_GOVERNANCE.md)).
- Reference this issue in your PR using keywords like `fixes #{issue_number}` for auto-closing.
- Tag a maintainer if you need review or triage.
- See [Contribution Guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Coding Standards](../instructions/coding-standards.instructions.md).
- For automation, labels, and issue types, review [AUTOMATION_GOVERNANCE.md](../AUTOMATION_GOVERNANCE.md).
